description: Quality corpus for AC-118: the same eight clips run-savings.mjs measures, each with four real recogniser transcripts (untrimmed baseline; the shipping module's output; and two controls) plus the authored reference each was spoken from. The criterion in run-quality.mjs reads this file offline and never calls a recogniser.

recogniser.request: POST /audio/transcriptions, response_format=json, language=<zh|en> from the clip name, no prompt
recogniser.throttle: 3200 ms minimum interval between calls (the out-of-tree client's own rate-limit gate)

provenance.recipe: One-off, out of tree: decode fixtures/<clip> with the runner's decodeWav, encode the four columns with the runner's encodeWav (baseline = the file itself; trimmed = trimVoiceAudio(samples, rate); flattened = trimVoiceAudio(..., { caps: FLATTENED_CAPS }); aggressive = trimVoiceAudio(..., AGGRESSIVE_TRIM)), post each encoded buffer to the recogniser, keep the returned text verbatim. The command and its date are recorded in the task's completion note. The generator is deliberately not in the repo: a committed criterion that can re-run the network is not an offline criterion, and the committed artefact is the frozen reading.
provenance.audioColumns: Each entry pins the sha256 of every encoded column. run-quality.mjs re-derives all four from the fixture wav through src/shared/voiceTrim.ts and requires the bytes to match, so "the trimmed transcript came from the shipping module's audio" is checked rather than asserted.
provenance.referenceSource: Authored scripts from the out-of-tree corpus generator tools/dictation-corpus.mjs (SCRIPTS / SCRIPTS_EN), verbatim — the text the TTS was given, so the reference is ground truth by construction.
provenance.composition: Eight clips: three Chinese occupancy tiers (o85 / o65 / o45) and two English, the same ladder run-savings.mjs uses. The transcripts are one take each, not an average.
